clue.text: Winger is a state, missing one shot ultimately

indicators.note: something missing a single item has lost the numeral one, written as the letter I

parts.note: taken as written
to state an opinion is to voice it

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the closing letter of the word is wanted

parts.note: the final letter of 'shot'

explanation.surface: A footballer on the wing is said to be in a state after missing a shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winger' looks like a footballer but means a bird. A VOICE loses its I (one) to give AVOCE, and T closes AVOCET.
explanation.definitionFit: The avocet is a wading bird with upturned bill, and crosswords often call any bird a winger since it flies.

clue.text: Palace player prone to histrionics a large supporter grabs

indicators.note: to grab is to seize and hold, so one piece closes around another

parts.note: taken as written
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
a ham is an actor who overacts
a bra is an undergarment that supports

explanation.surface: A Crystal Palace footballer given to diving is grabbed by a big fan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Palace' looks like the London football club Crystal Palace, but it is the Moorish palace in Granada. A, L and BRA hold HAM.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alhambra is the famous Moorish palace and fortress complex in Granada, southern Spain.

clue.text: When to have rumpy-pumpy? After serving up wine!

indicators.note: one piece is placed after another, so they are simply set side by side

parts.note: 'as' can mean 'when', as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading from the bottom, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: 'it' is a coy word for sex

explanation.surface: A cheeky question about when to have sex, answered: after serving the wine.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark splits the surface, but the wordplay runs straight across it. Rumpy-pumpy is British slang for sex, and 'it' is the coy word for the act.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling Italian white from Piedmont, a frequent crossword wine.

clue.text: Man and his best friend touring uni by a lake

indicators.note: to tour a place is to go all round it, so one piece surrounds another

parts.note: a dog is man's best friend
U is short for university
taken as written
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A man walks his dog round a university campus beside a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his' refers back to the defining word: man's best friend is DOG, which tours U, then A and L follow. Dougal is also the dog in The Magic Roundabout, a British children's programme.
explanation.definitionFit: Dougal is a Scottish masculine first name, so it is an example of a man's name.

clue.text: Sentence given to a grasping English type like Jeffrey Archer

parts.note: a life sentence, the maximum prison term

indicators.note: to grasp is to clutch in the hand, so one piece holds another inside it

parts.note: 'a' means 'per', as in 'five pounds a head'
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A greedy Englishman like Jeffrey Archer gets a prison sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls Archer's real jail term for perjury. 'a' is PER, which grasps E to make PEER.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeffrey Archer, the novelist and politician, sits in the House of Lords by appointment for his lifetime, not by inheritance.

clue.text: Horny blighter really enjoyed being turned over

indicators.note: something turned over is flipped end to end, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: to have really lived is to have enjoyed life to the full

explanation.surface: A randy rogue revels in being bedded and rolled over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horny' suggests lust, but it is literal: the devil is pictured with horns.
explanation.definitionFit: The devil is traditionally drawn with horns, and blighter is British slang for a rascal or wretch.

clue.text: Party girl mostly seen around high-class German capital

indicators.note: to be seen around something is to be found surrounding it, so one piece wraps another
mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party
a lass is a girl
U means upper-class, as in U and non-U
G is the abbreviation for German

explanation.surface: A party girl is spotted round a posh German capital such as Berlin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German capital' looks like one phrase naming Berlin, but German only supplies its abbreviation and the definition is the bare word 'capital'.
explanation.definitionFit: Douglas is the capital town of the Isle of Man, the self-governing island in the Irish Sea.

clue.text: Somewhat quiet last section of Miles's Kind of Blue

indicators.note: the last section of a word is its closing letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the possessive
feeling blue is feeling low
the suffix -ish means 'kind of', as in reddish

explanation.surface: The closing track of Miles Davis's album Kind of Blue is rather hushed.
explanation.walkthrough: The italic album title looks like one unit, but it splits in two, and the suffix from 'Kind of' is written after the word for 'Blue'.
explanation.definitionFit: Business that is slow is quiet, with few customers, and the suffix softens it to fairly so.

clue.text: You are one with nasty odour and must repel date

parts.note: a hum is British slang for a bad smell

indicators.note: to repel something is to drive it away, so that letter is pushed out

parts.note: taken as written
D is the abbreviation for date

explanation.surface: Someone with bad body odour is told they will put off any romantic date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'date' looks like a partner on an evening out, but it is just its abbreviation, pushed out of the word 'and'.
explanation.definitionFit: Addressed to the reader, it is true: every solver is a person, a member of our species.

clue.text: Picking up gun, rich sap gets the shakes

indicators.note: something shaken is jumbled up, so its letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A wealthy fool buying a firearm starts trembling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picking up gun' reads as one action, but the definition stops at 'Picking up'; the gun belongs to the letters being mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick something up can mean to buy it, as in picking up a bargain at the shops.

clue.text: Award Jesus stuck on Hoskins after a change of ways

indicators.note: something stuck on is attached to the end, so one piece follows another
a change of way means a change of direction, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: the setter, Hoskins, refers to himself as me
both 'Jesus!' and 'My!' are exclamations of surprise

explanation.surface: The setter claims a prize after Jesus changes his ways and joins him.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often name themselves for ME. 'Jesus' is not a person here but the exclamation, swapped for its milder cousin MY.
explanation.definitionFit: The Emmy is the American television industry's annual prize, a statuette given for excellence in TV.

clue.text: A soft and thick congealed lump of dope

definitions.text: A soft and thick congealed lump
definitions.meaning: first meaning: a semi-solid mass, as of blood

explanation.surface: A small sticky lump of cannabis resin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soft' and 'thick' both also mean stupid, steering towards the second sense; and 'dope' pretends to be the drug. Clot is mild British slang for an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: Blood forms a jelly-like mass when it sets, and a dim-witted person can be called by the same word in Britain.

clue.text: Times everybody will go to medium without any doubt

parts.note: three by four means three times four
all means everyone
a medium is a means of communication or expression

explanation.surface: At times everyone will certainly consult a spiritualist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper, and 'medium' like a psychic; both are their dictionary second senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an emphatic yes, granting permission or agreeing certainly, so it signals no hesitation at all.

clue.text: A bit off the back of dormer caught burglar's tongue

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a bit taken from the back end is the closing letter only

parts.note: the final letter of 'dormer'
to have got someone is to have caught them

explanation.surface: A burglar is caught breaking a piece off a dormer window.
explanation.walkthrough: A dormer is a window jutting from a sloping roof, the burglar's way in. 'tongue' means language, not a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: Argot is the secret slang of a group, originally the cant used among thieves and criminals.

clue.text: Yours truly will punch senior teacher

indicators.note: to punch is to pierce or knock a hole in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: Sr is the abbreviation for senior
the setter speaking of themselves

explanation.surface: The setter threatens to hit a senior member of staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'senior teacher' reads as one job title, but 'senior' gives SR and 'teacher' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: British pupils address a male schoolmaster as sir, so the form of address stands for the teacher himself.

clue.text: Investigation ruined Archer, Evening Standard originally admitted

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked out of shape, so its letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: originally means at the beginning, so each word gives only its first letter

parts.note: the opening letters of the paper's two words

explanation.surface: A newspaper owns up that its inquiry ruined Jeffrey Archer.
explanation.walkthrough: The Evening Standard is London's evening newspaper. Its initials are taken in among the letters before the whole lot is mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: Research is systematic study to establish facts, which is what an investigation sets out to do.

clue.text: Rowdy type seen with a motorcycle messenger

definitions.text: Rowdy type seen with a motorcycle
definitions.meaning: first meaning: a member of a notorious motorcycle gang whose name begins with Hells
second meaning: a bearer of divine messages

explanation.surface: A hooligan on a motorbike works as a courier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'motorcycle messenger' looks like a courier; it splits into a biker-gang member and the Greek-derived word for messenger.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek angelos meant envoy, and Hells Angels members are known individually by the same word.

clue.text: Broadcaster's description of head of SEAT's charity?

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of the car maker's name

indicators.note: a broadcaster speaks words over the air, so we go by what is heard

parts.note: the capital letters of the brand show a big S at its start

explanation.surface: A radio presenter describes a car company's charitable giving.
explanation.walkthrough: SEAT is a Spanish car maker, printed in capitals; its first letter is a large S, and saying that phrase gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Largesse is generous giving of money or gifts, the open-handedness that charity shows.

clue.text: Ruddy cut, having necked last of molly and grass

indicators.note: to neck is British slang for to swallow, so one piece goes down inside another
a cut word has been trimmed, losing its final letter

parts.note: ruddy means red-faced

indicators.note: the last of a word is its closing letter alone

parts.note: the final letter of 'molly'

explanation.surface: A flushed reveller cut up after swallowing some Molly and cannabis.
explanation.walkthrough: Molly and grass look like drugs (ecstasy and marijuana), but 'grass' is the definition. RED loses its D and swallows Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Rye is a cereal plant of the grass family, grown for grain and whisky.

clue.text: Designate rake perverted after cuddling lively ram

indicators.note: to cuddle is to hug something close, so one piece wraps around another
something perverted is twisted out of its proper form, so its letters are reshaped

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

indicators.note: lively suggests jumping about, so these letters move into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A depraved libertine is pointed out after embracing a frisky ram.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rake' looks like a garden tool or a womaniser; both words are just letters, each mixed, one hugging the other.
explanation.definitionFit: To earmark is to set aside or designate for a purpose, from marking an animal's ear to show its owner.

clue.text: Lawyer ultimately probing model at High Court?

indicators.note: to probe is to poke inside, so one piece goes into another

parts.note: to model is to pose for an artist

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the closing letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of 'Lawyer'

indicators.note: someone high is intoxicated and all over the place, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A barrister at the High Court cross-examines a model in the witness box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lawyer' does double duty in the surface but is the definition; its last letter alone probes POSE. 'High Court' looks like one name, but 'High' scrambles COURT.
explanation.definitionFit: A prosecutor is the lawyer who brings and conducts the case against a defendant in a criminal trial.

clue.text: A Parisian enthralled by game Penny's approach

indicators.note: something enthralled is held captive, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: RU is short for Rugby Union
un is French for 'a'
p is the abbreviation for a penny

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman is captivated by Penny's game plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penny' looks like a woman's name, but it is the coin. Rugby Union is the game, and the French article sits between its two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A run-up is the approach to something, as a bowler's run before delivering or the lead-up to an event.

clue.text: Briefly get on well with European eating hot chestnut?

indicators.note: said briefly, the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: two people who click get on well
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: Getting on with a European who is eating hot roast chestnuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hot chestnut' reads as street food, but 'hot' gives H and 'chestnut' alone, with its question mark, is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An old chestnut is a stale joke or story told too often, much like a worn-out phrase.

clue.text: Writer of national importance blackballed in hearing

indicators.note: in hearing means as perceived by the ear, so we go by sound not spelling

parts.note: to be blackballed is to be barred from membership

explanation.surface: An eminent national author is rejected by a club at a hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hearing' looks like a tribunal, which suits blackballing, but it signals sound. The Bard is Shakespeare, England's national poet.
explanation.definitionFit: A bard is a poet, and with the article it means Shakespeare, the country's most celebrated writer.

clue.text: Song and dance made this crossword writer put out

indicators.note: to put someone out is to eject them, so those letters are removed

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance
taken as written
the setter speaking of himself

explanation.surface: The setter was annoyed at being made to sing and dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Song and dance' looks like a fuss, but 'Song' alone is the definition, and the setter takes himself out of 'made'.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballad is a narrative song or a slow sentimental popular song, so it is a kind of song.

clue.text: Old person about to break hip getting bit of action

indicators.note: to break into something is to enter it, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: hip and in both mean fashionable
c, for circa, means about

indicators.note: a small bit of a word here is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of 'action'

explanation.surface: An elderly person is about to break a hip while getting some exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old person' reads as a pensioner but means a member of an ancient people. IN plus A is broken by C.
explanation.definitionFit: The Incas were the people of the pre-Columbian empire in Peru, so an Inca is a person from the past.

clue.text: Hence trial off?

indicators.note: something off has gone bad or wrong, so these letters are out of their proper order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the two words rearranged, and the situation of a defendant whose trial has been called off.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone no longer under suspicion or free from danger is safe, which a dropped prosecution leaves them.

clue.text: Drug test requires reviewing weighty reading material

indicators.note: to review is to look back over, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
the MOT is Britain's annual roadworthiness test for cars

explanation.surface: A drug trial demands reading through a heavy report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reviewing' looks like reading, which suits the surface, but it turns E and MOT round together.
explanation.definitionFit: A tome is a large, heavy and usually scholarly book, the kind that is hard going to read.

clue.text: Posh hubby drops billion for parking in London area

indicators.note: dropping one thing for another means swapping it out, so one letter replaces another

parts.note: David Beckham is the husband of Victoria, Posh Spice
B is the abbreviation for billion
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A rich husband gives up a fortune for a parking space in London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Posh' looks like an adjective but is Posh Spice of the Spice Girls, whose husband is the footballer David Beckham.
explanation.definitionFit: Peckham is a district of south-east London, in the borough of Southwark.

clue.text: Fiery emission from box close to firework

parts.note: to spar is to box in practice

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only the final letter is wanted

parts.note: the final letter of 'firework'

explanation.surface: Flames shoot out of a box of fireworks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'box' looks like a container, but it is the verb, as in boxing.
explanation.definitionFit: A spark is a tiny burning particle thrown off by a fire or firework.
